correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge2\), every real \(0<s\le2\), and every \(p\ge0\), the exact powered-distance matrix has fiber-difference eigenvalue \(-s^p\), two copies of \(E_1=m(a-b2^p)+(m-1)s^p\le-1\), and two copies of \(E_2=m(-b+a2^p)+(m-1)s^p\) on the zero-sum subspace. The critical eigenvalue satisfies \(E_2(0)=-1\), is strictly convex, and tends to positive infinity, yielding exactly one positive zero and exactly two null directions at the endpoint. The centered Gram rank follows. The equation \(m h_s(p)=s^p\) and strict convexity give three scaling regimes, with \(h_s(0)=h_s'(0)=0\) at \(s=2^{-a}\) and \(h_s''(0)=(\log2)^2\). Independently reconstructed full distance matrices passed 210 spectral tests, 725 exact identities, and 48 boundary tests; proof is analytic, not an extrapolation.

value.rationale: The family connects two canonical graph blow-ups of \(C_5\) by a continuous weighted metric parameter. The exact exponent and critical Euclidean rank give a complete natural two-parameter Hilbert snowflake classification. The sharp intracluster threshold separates positive limiting roundness from \(m^{-1}\) collapse; the unique critical point instead has an \(m^{-1/2}\) law with explicit coefficient. This differentiates distinct embedding-stability regimes and cannot be read off a single finite example, a routine bound, or the known ordinary \(C_5\) calculation.
